title: Informed Consent Form: Tap-to-Adapt Online Study of Adaptive Speech Interaction and Personalized Response Timing

study_name: Tap-to-Adapt: Online Study of Adaptive Speech Interaction and Personalized Response Timing
typed_name_help: Please type your real name. Under this consent form, your typed name, on-screen acknowledgment, consent-form version, and server timestamp together constitute your recorded electronic informed consent. A handwritten signature on paper is not required for online participation.

sections.heading: Description of the Project
paragraphs: This study is conducted under the research institution's approved human research ethics protocol for adaptive speech interaction and human–agent collaboration. Within the approved ethics scope, the project examines how adaptive models affect interaction timing, correction burden, user experience, trust, safety, and system performance.

The present implementation (Tap-to-Adapt) studies whether shared priors and online personalization reduce the need for manual activation/interruption when interacting with a speech-based agent, and how adaptation affects perceived predictability and control. The study is for research evaluation only and is not used for identity recognition or high-stakes decisions.

sections.heading: Description of the Study
paragraphs: This is a remote online study using a dedicated research system in your browser, together with microphone input on your own device. After electronic consent and screening, you will complete a scheduled interactive session of about 30 minutes of effective interaction: five six-minute active blocks with a fixed one-minute rest between adjacent blocks. Within each block you typically talk with the experimental system on the computer for four minutes and then with the companion agent on the phone for two minutes. The timed flow lasts about 34 minutes. Device checks and the final questionnaire take place outside the timed interaction.

During the session you will speak with research agents/systems and may manually activate or interrupt responses when timing feels wrong. You may be assigned to a condition such as cold-start personalization, shared-model frozen behavior, or shared-model online personalization; condition names may be blinded during the study.

After the session you will complete short questionnaires about predictability, control, correctability, and related experience. Optional follow-up or dataset-related choices, if any, will be presented separately and may be declined without losing basic eligibility or basic compensation.

Participation remains within the approved participation-time limits (for example, no more than 120 minutes per visit and no more than 60 minutes of active speech/multimodal interaction per visit, with appropriate breaks).

sections.heading: Risks
paragraphs: We do not anticipate any greater than minimal risks from participating in this research study. Risks are comparable to ordinary use of voice assistants or online meetings. Possible discomforts include voice or eye strain, fatigue, frustration with mistimed responses, privacy concerns about voice recordings, incidental capture of background speech, or concern about re-identification from audio.

To minimize risks, only approved research audio/interaction data will be collected; raw voice data are treated as identifiable or potentially identifiable and segregated from routine coded datasets; you will be asked to use a reasonably private setting and avoid saying names, contact details, or sensitive information; rest breaks are provided; and you may pause or withdraw at any time without penalty.

sections.heading: Benefits
paragraphs: Findings may improve adaptive speech agents and reduce unnecessary manual correction in future interactive systems. You may experience a research speech interface and contribute to academic evaluation of personalization methods. There is no guarantee of direct personal benefit beyond the study experience and any compensation described below.

sections.heading: Compensation
paragraphs: If you complete the required study activities for this enrollment, you will receive a fixed compensation of RMB 40, as disclosed at recruitment. This amount is within the approved compensation ceiling (up to RMB 50 per hour and no more than RMB 400 per enrollment occasion). Partial compensation will be based on time or completed required activities and will not depend on optional recording/reuse choices or study outcomes.

sections.heading: Voluntary Participation
paragraphs: Participation in this research is completely voluntary. You may refuse to participate, may withdraw at any time without providing a reason, and may decline to answer any question—all without negative consequences for your academic evaluation, employment assessment, or future opportunities to join other studies.

Core study participation requires collection of interaction timing/events and related coded measures needed for the research questions. Saving raw audio, future reuse, controlled sharing, or public release of speech-related materials—if offered—are optional layered choices. Declining any optional choice will not affect basic compensation.

If you withdraw, you may request deletion of identifiers, coded study data, and (where still feasible) study audio until 14 days after your final participation (or such other 7/14/30-day deadline as locked in the Implementation Record and shown at consent). After irreversible de-identification, incorporation into aggregate results, or incorporation into a trained model after that deadline, removal may no longer be possible.

sections.heading: Personal Privacy and Data Confidentiality
paragraphs: The information collected will not be publicly disclosed in a way that a specific person can be identified unless you expressly consent or disclosure is required by law. Every reasonable precaution will be taken in relation to the storage, use, and disposition of data.

By participating in the study, you understand and agree that the the research institution (the research institution) may be required to disclose your consent record, data, and other personally identifiable information as required by law, regulation, subpoena, or court order. Otherwise, your confidentiality will be maintained as follows:

Your research data and consent/compensation records will be kept separately. Consent and compensation records will be stored in locked or encrypted institutional records and will not be disclosed to third parties except as required by law or institutional audit. By participating, you understand and agree that coded data and information gathered during this study may be used by the research institution and published and/or disclosed by the research institution to others outside of the research institution for academic purposes. However, your name, address, contact information, and other direct personal identifiers will not be mentioned in any such publication or dissemination of the research data and/or results by the research institution.

The researchers will take the following steps to protect participants' identities: (1) each participant will be assigned a study code; (2) researchers will record research data by code, not by name; (3) only authorized members of the research group will view identifiable linkage or compensation records in detail; (4) electronic research data will be stored on encrypted, access-controlled systems.

Study-specific data for this consent implementation may include: coded screening/demographic, language/accent, and experience data; raw or derived audio/speech data where you consent to the applicable recording choice; transcripts after screening; interaction timing, turn-taking, correction, and system-state events; questionnaires and fatigue ratings; model scores, outputs, updates, and participant-specific adaptive state; and technical/quality logs. Contact and compensation records are stored separately.

Raw face/voice recordings are identifiable or potentially identifiable and will not be publicly released in identifiable form under this consent. Any broader sharing or dataset release would require the specific optional consent choices disclosed for that purpose. Research data status is coded, not anonymous, unless a specific derived release is irreversibly de-identified as separately disclosed.

sections.heading: University reimbursement details and electronic-signature choice
paragraphs: Collection basis: the University's standard financial reimbursement requirements. To pay and reimburse the RMB 40 compensation for completing the full interaction and final questionnaire through the University's finance process, the page asks after informed consent and before the study whether you are willing to provide a full name, Mainland resident identity-card number (or another approved document if you do not have one), and a handwritten electronic signature. Identity-document numbers and electronic signatures are high-risk personal information.

These reimbursement-identity data are encrypted at the application layer into a separate compensation-identity vault and are linked to the research process only through a random participant ID. Their plaintext is absent from the research event database, questionnaire database, speech and personal models, research analysis, and generic administrator export.

Purpose: payment and reimbursement of study compensation only. Recipients: authorised compensation staff on the research team and the University's finance department. Retention: according to the University's financial-record retention requirements. These data will not be used for research analysis, model training, or dataset release.

If you do not trust or do not wish to provide a name, identity-card number, and handwritten signature, you may explicitly choose not to provide them and continue the study. The system stores only that choice, the notice version, and the time, not those identity details. This choice does not affect study eligibility or the base RMB 40 compensation. After completion, contact WeChat study-contact (WeChat name: Research team) so that the research team can arrange an alternative payment method that does not require submitting these details. Note: the typed name required by the consent form belongs to the electronic informed-consent record and is independent of these optional reimbursement-identity details.

sections.heading: Coercion and Undue Influence
paragraphs: There will be no coercion or undue influence. You may stop your participation at any time without explanation. Declining optional data-use choices (where offered) will not affect your eligibility or basic compensation.

sections.heading: Consent
paragraphs: This study uses explicit electronic (online) informed consent. After reading this form, you will be asked to confirm the statement below by checking an on-screen consent box and typing your name. Your confirmation, together with the consent-form version identifier and a server timestamp, constitutes your recorded informed consent. A handwritten signature on paper is not required for online participation.
You will be asked to confirm this consent form, which states:

“I have read and fully understood what is stated in this consent form, and I am willing to participate in this study. I understand that my electronic confirmation (typed name, on-screen acknowledgment, consent version, and timestamp) constitutes my recorded informed consent.”
